long_biography.plain_text:
Gottlieb earned a bachelor's degree from Miami University and a law degree from Northwestern before joining the Illinois bar in the late 1960s. He then spent eight years inside two major financial institutions, gaining a lender's-eye view of credit transactions. Back in private practice, his assignments ranged from collateral documentation to receiverships and Chapter 11 matters.

At Chuhak & Tecson, Gottlieb and Josh Hyman launched a dedicated banking practice in 2002. The group grew through the financial crisis into a national team serving more than 100 institutions. He also served on the firm's Finance Committee and spent years on the board of Family Focus, a Chicago nonprofit supporting children and families. The organisation now lists him among its life members.
